ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L. 561-1 et seq. and R. 561-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier); Articles L. 123-1 et seq., L. 123-223 et seq. and R. 123-223 et seq. of the French Commercial Code (Code de commerce); Décret n° 2016-567 of 10 May 2016 (UBO register); Loi n° 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Loi Sapin II); EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843 and Regulation (EU) 2024/1640; French FIU supervision by Tracfin.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs is held by the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés via INPI; general public access was suspended following the CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022, C-37/20 and C-601/20; access is limited to competent authorities, AML/CFT obliged entities performing customer due diligence, and persons demonstrating a legitimate interest)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing and company extract of the non-resident corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry in the country of origin (e.g., Registrar of Companies, Chamber of Commerce, or Notary Chamber)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if the origin state is party to the 1961 Hague Convention) OR French Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copies of identity documents (passport, residence permit where relevant) of the proposed SARL manager(s) and ultimate beneficial owner(s)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent public officer in the country of origin, followed by the competent origin-state authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR French Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation (traduction assermentée) of foreign corporate and identity documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court-appointed certified translator (traducteur expert inscrit auprès d'une Cour d'appel française)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic certification by the expert translator before the originating French court; no Hague apostille required for the French certificate itself

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney authorizing the French avocat or founding agent to sign and file the incorporation documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or French Consulate in the country of origin (with legalization of signature where required)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR French Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds confirmation covering the capital contribution and initial working funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Origin-country credit institution providing correspondent banking reference
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille OR French Consular Legalization where required by the receiving French bank

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, managers, and authorized signatories against Tracfin (French FIU), the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN List, and the French National Freezing List (AGEA-FI). Capital contributors must evidence source of funds. Screening results are documented and retained for five years in accordance with Article L. 561-45 of the French Monetary and Financial Code, and re-executed at bank account opening, at each transaction threshold, and upon any change in beneficial ownership.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises operated by the INPI (guichet-entreprises.service-public.fr), feeding the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RNCS) and the local Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SARL dénomination sociale must be reproduced exclusively in Latin characters; any foreign-script or non-Latin name must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet before filing. The name must be capable of clear reproduction in French commercial documents and must not be confusingly identical or similar to an existing RNCS-registered entity or to a prior trademark registered with INPI or EUIPO for identical or similar activities.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not maintain a statutory stand-alone name reservation; availability is validated pre-submission against INPI and RNCS databases, with 30 days used as the internal pre-validation window before filing. If the Guichet Unique rejects the incorporation filing on name-conflict or public-order grounds, the filer may correct and resubmit the dossier free of additional filing fee within the same registered-account session. Where the rejection is substantive, the applicant may (i) file a hierarchical petition (recours gracieux) addressed to the INPI director within two months of notification, (ii) apply to the President of the Commercial Court of the registered office seat (référé) for an order against refusal, and (iii) where the conflict arises from a third-party trademark, initiate opposition before INPI or cancellation proceedings before the French courts.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Expressly permissible. A SARL may contract with a licensed commercial domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) under Article L. 123-11-2 of the French Commercial Code for a maximum renewable period of five years. The company is required to maintain genuine administrative substance at the domiciled address, including receipt of mail, availability of statutory records, and access for authorities. Virtual office is accepted for non-regulated logistics brokerage (ISIC 5229) provided the activity does not trigger warehousing or freight-forwarding operational permits requiring physical premises.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low. Quantified at approximately 5% per annum for a non-regulated, low-risk logistics SARL in the absence of tax, AML, or customs red flags. Ordinary tax audits (vérification de comptabilité) require prior written notice; unannounced physical inspection occurs only through criminal-search warrants (perquisition) in exceptional fraud or sanctions cases.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the French Articles of Association (statuts) in French by an avocat, including UBO and governance clauses
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for standard SARL incorporation (EUR 1,200-EUR 2,500 for multi-UBO and tax-driven structures)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the legal incorporation notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Authorized French legal announcements gazette (e.g., Les Échos, Petites Affiches)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per announcement line count, approximately EUR 80-EUR 150 for a standard small-format notice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Guichet Unique / RNCS registration and incorporation filing fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI and Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (collected through the Guichet Unique)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff revised annually (approximately EUR 40-EUR 50 for SARL creation without branches)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: INPI administrative processing and company-file setup (formalities handling)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administrative fee for RNE record creation and Kbis issuance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Blocked capital deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt de capital) issued by the deposit-taking bank or notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French credit institution or notaire (or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations for regulated professions)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing bank tariff of EUR 0-EUR 250 per certificate, depending on institution and AML/KYC workload

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of foreign corporate registry documents, UBO identification documents, and powers of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Court-appointed certified translator (traducteur expert près la cour d'appel)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 70-EUR 120 per standard page; estimated 4-6 pages for a two-shareholder foreign structure

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of foreign-origin corporate and identity documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of the origin state and/or French Consular Section
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Convention tariff or consular fee of EUR 15-EUR 80 per document; estimated 3-5 documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial domiciliation of the registered office (first quarter fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed commercial domiciliation company (société de domiciliation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of EUR 60-EUR 150 per month, including mail handling, statutory records hosting, and lease of corporate seat

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 et seq. (SARL); formation and registration provisions include Articles L.210-1 et seq. and R.123-1 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent local clerk of the Commercial Court (greffe du tribunal de commerce) maintains the Trade and Companies Register (Registre du commerce et des sociétés, RCS). Formation filings are submitted through the INPI-operated Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic declaration of business creation and supporting documents filed through the Guichet unique; the SARL's signed articles of association (statuts) are a mandatory supporting instrument. The former paper M0 form is not the standard filing route.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies. At least 20% of cash contributions must be paid on incorporation; the balance must be paid within five years of registration. Cash contributions are deposited with an authorized bank, notary, or other legally authorized depositary, and released after RCS registration. Contributions in kind are fully contributed at formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accepts the subscriptions set out in its executed articles of association and acknowledges payment of the required initial cash contributions. RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at [full French address], subject to evidence of the right to occupy those premises. RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed gérant (manager) for an indefinite term, with authority to represent and bind the Company within applicable law and the articles. RESOLVED, that the gérant is authorized to complete registration, obtain the Company’s identifiers, open operating accounts, and undertake all filings and administrative steps necessary to commence the stated business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute the SARL articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders and, where applicable, a French notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Set the corporate name, registered office, purpose, duration, capital, share allocations, management provisions, and appointment of the gérant. Execute the articles; use a notarial deed where a contribution or transaction legally requires notarization. Obtain certified French translations of foreign-language supporting documents where needed.
required_dossiers: Draft and final articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistencies between the articles, subscription evidence, and filing data; re-execute amended articles and obtain required signatures or notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit cash capital and document contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized depositary bank, notary, or other legally authorized depositary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital-deposit account, pay at least 20% of each cash contribution, and obtain the certificate of deposit. Document any contribution in kind and obtain a commissaire aux apports report when required by law, unless a valid statutory exemption applies.
required_dossiers: Executed articles or draft articles accepted by the depositary
Founder identification and beneficial-owner information requested by the depositary
Contribution-in-kind valuation report or exemption decision, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve bank KYC or source-of-funds queries with certified ownership and funds evidence; correct subscription amounts and obtain a replacement deposit certificate if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized legal-announcement publication service in the département of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the prescribed formation notice and retain the publication certificate for the Guichet unique filing. Ensure that the notice matches the executed articles, including company name, legal form, capital, address, purpose, duration, and gérant.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Publish a corrective notice if required particulars are missing or inconsistent; attach the corrected certificate to the registration filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the creation filing and beneficial-owner declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises; registration processed by the competent local RCS clerk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic creation declaration with signed articles and supporting evidence. Identify beneficial owners and file the required beneficial-ownership information. Pay applicable registry and filing charges; the USD fee stated above is an approximate conversion of the standard RCS filing charge and is not a fixed all-in amount.
required_dossiers: Foreign corporate-founder documents, apostille or legalization, and French translations, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to a Guichet unique or RCS deficiency notice within its stated deadline, upload corrected or missing documents, and pay any additional assessed charge. Challenge a formal refusal through the competent registry or court procedure where appropriate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique, competent tax office, social-security authorities, and depositary bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain and verify the SIREN/SIRET and Kbis extract, then provide registration evidence to the depositary to release capital. Complete applicable tax and employer registrations, maintain statutory registers and accounting records, and display required company particulars on business documents.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract or current RCS registration evidence
Tax and employer-registration information, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct identifier or registration-data errors through the Guichet unique and RCS clerk; promptly complete any outstanding tax, social, or bank KYC requests.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No general industrial licensing board is required for a SARL providing project-cargo logistics coordination. The competent authorities depend on the activities performed: DREAL (Direction régionale de l’environnement, de l’aménagement et du logement) for relevant road-transport and regulated-facility matters; the prefecture and local authorities for route-specific exceptional-transport permissions.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general manufacturing or industrial operating permit. If the company itself conducts regulated road haulage for hire, it may require registration in the transport register and a Community licence or other applicable road-transport authorization; a freight-forwarding commissionnaire de transport activity may require registration in the register of transport and freight-forwarding operators. Exceptional-load movements require applicable route and vehicle authorizations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition (Ministère de la Transition écologique); regional implementation is generally through the DREAL and the prefecture
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: No EIA is ordinarily required solely for logistics coordination. A depot, terminal, workshop, storage site, or other physical installation must be screened under the Environmental Code and applicable ICPE nomenclature; an EIA, environmental authorization, registration, or declaration may be required depending on the project and thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: There is no single sector-wide numerical threshold for this business scope. Comply with any ICPE authorization, applicable water-law requirements, local wastewater-discharge permit and sewer conditions, and applicable air-emission limits. Segregate, classify, store, and transfer waste through authorized channels, with traceability and hazardous-waste documentation where required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No universal pre-opening fire or structural certificate applies to an office-only logistics company. Premises open to the public may require ERP fire and accessibility compliance and approvals under applicable rules. Warehouses and workshops must meet applicable building, fire-safety, workplace, and ICPE requirements; structural capacity must be suitable for intended loads. Employers must complete occupational risk assessment and prevention measures, including the required DUERP.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA)

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), acting within the Eurosystem; prudential banking supervision is delegated to the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR). Foreign-exchange regulatory policy and external financial relations reporting are administratively coordinated by the Direction Générale du Trésor of the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: As a euro-area member, France maintains full currency convertibility for both current-account and capital-account transactions under EU law, particularly Articles 63 and 64 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. Non-resident shareholders may freely repatriate dividends, branch profits, liquidation proceeds and sale-of-ownership proceeds without previous exchange-control authorization. Profit remittance from a French SARL is not blocked by currency rules, but continues to be subject to ordinary French withholding taxes (default 25% on dividend distributions, subject to reduction under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or applicable double-tax treaties) and to standard anti-money-laundering verification of the underlying economic purpose. The only convertibility-related requirements are statistical balance-of-payment declarations to the Banque de France for direct investment positions crossing defined reporting thresholds and the bank-driven transmission of cross-border cash-flow details for monetary statistics.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France does not impose any statutory surrender or mandatory conversion of export receipts. A French exporting SARL may invoice and collect in any freely convertible currency and retain proceeds in euro or foreign-currency accounts. There is no prescribed settlement timeline for converting repatriated export proceeds, and any mandatory conversion ratio is nil. The residual regulatory duties are limited to the periodic balance-of-payments reporting obligation under the French external financial relations regulation, triggered when the aggregate cross-border flows exceed published thresholds, together with the need to present the bank with the governing transport and project-cargo contracts for AML/KYC purposes when funds are received.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore non-EU digital EMIs have low banking viability in France unless they are registered or passported under the Payment Services Directive (PSD2) and are supervised by the ACPR. The SARL may only lawfully use an EMI account for principal treasury flows when the provider holds a French payment institution licence or an EU passport with an ACPR relationship. Such an EMI can be used efficiently for cross-border customer payments and multi-currency settlement, but its long-term availability for milestone and LC transaction flows is narrower than that of a full tier-1 bank. Overall feasibility: High for an EU-licensed EMI with a French IBAN and ACPR notification; Low for any offshore provider without a valid EU passport because it creates sanctions, recovery and audit risks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a French SARL, the legal representative (gérant) and each ultimate beneficial owner must submit to full KYC/AML due diligence under Articles L561-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code. Physical presence at a branch remains the standard reference for first-time onboarding, although most tier-1 French banks now accept a remote video interview for low-risk non-complex corporate clients when all corporate documents are notarised, apostilled and certified. Remote opening is therefore possible at the bank's discretion but is not a statutory right; the bank may lawfully require a face-to-face interview whenever it assesses elevated risk. For a SARL controlled by non-resident directors, the standard documentation pack includes an original Kbis extract, articles of association (statuts), UBO declaration, valid passports, proof of residential address, business references and, where applicable, a source-of-funds certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain is opaque or contains a shareholder domiciled in a high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of passports of directors and ultimate shareholders; formal UBO declaration under Article L.561-2-2 of the French Monetary and Financial Code; chain-of-ownership diagram from the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); audited financial statements and bank references of the investor; written explanation of the commercial and treasury rationale for the shareholder's jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening or negative-media alert connected to the cargo logistics chain, especially an OOG heavy-haul project route that touches or transits a sanctioned or embargoed territory.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions-screening results demonstrating no match or a cleared match; project-cargo route map with stated ports and transshipment points; export/import licences; end-user certificates; transport insurance cover notes; charter-party agreements, bills of lading, cargo manifests and packing lists evidencing the physical movement of goods through legitimate corridors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment-flow mismatch: the milestone-wire and LC values appear inconsistent with the low-risk project-cargo turnover or with invoices submitted for a young SARL.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed project-logistics service contracts; client purchase orders; a rolling invoice-and-milestone registry; cash-flow forecast; pre-financing supply-chain explanations; French audited or management accounts; VAT and corporation-tax returns demonstrating the economic substance of the expected cash flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or offshore parent structure appears to have limited economic substance and may indicate channel-company or conduit arrangements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group organisational chart; board minutes and management accounts of the non-resident parent; evidence of business substance (office lease, payroll, operating licence); latest audited financial statements; tax-residency certificate from the parent's jurisdiction; French legal opinion confirming that the SARL's management exercises its decision-making independently and that projections are consistent with the logistics business plan.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections into the French SARL should be remitted by SWIFT MT103 from the parent's corporate bank, referencing the ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQUI' or 'INVE' (equity capital/investment) together with an explicit remittance note citing the share-capital increase or shareholder current account. The receiving French bank performs sanctions screening, AML verification and source-of-funds checks; the injection must correspond to the subscribed capital in the notarial or corporate registration documentation. If the capital injection amounts to a qualifying direct investment, the French SARL or investor must file the applicable balance-of-payment declaration with the Banque de France, including post-closing reporting where the statutory thresholds are exceeded. The verification gate requires board resolution, subscribed-share confirmation, a signed bank order, and proof of the investor's identity and economic substance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Treasury disbursements for project-cargo heavy-haul operations will be cleared through three principal rails: (1) SEPA Credit Transfer using ISO 20022 pacs.008 messages for euro payments within the EEA; (2) SWIFT MT103 for non-euro or non-EEA counterparty payments, with the transaction quoted in the original currency and converted at a transparent market-based rate; and (3) Commercial Letter of Credit under UCP 600 opened/appointed via SWIFT MT700/MT707 messages for equipment procurement or for major client milestone settlements. All outbound disbursements must be supported by the underlying project-cargo contract, invoices from subcontractors or port and haulage vendors, and adequate proof of transport service execution. The bank applies currency conversion at prevailing interbank rates plus a margin, and may require trade documentation (bills of lading, CMRs, customs declarations) before releasing proceeds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forward (EUR/USD or EUR/GBP) concluded with an ACPR-regulated bank or passported EU bank under the applicable ISDA/EMIR framework
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) for currencies subject to convertibility restrictions or for currencies where local settlement in the target jurisdiction is unavailable
Cross-currency swap (CCIS) to hedge both FX and interest-rate exposure arising from project milestone receivables and supplier payables in different currencies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties of 0.5% of annual turnover per month of delay, capped at 5% of CA; risk of administrative strike-off for prolonged non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Financial Statements (Bilan and Compte de Résultat)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 15th day of the 4th month following fiscal year-end (e.g., 15 June for calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to 0.5% of CA per month of delay, maximum 5% of CA; potential company strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form IS1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 15th day of the 4th month following fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties and interest on late payments; risk of administrative sanctions including strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent statutory audit if annual turnover exceeds €800,000
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (PCG) per Code de Commerce

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual declaration of Ultimate Beneficial Owners to the French tax authorities (DGFiP) via online portal; required confirmation of no changes in ownership structure

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: €80 - €250 annually for registered office and corporate agent services in France
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: €0 if no mandatory audit required; €1,500 - €4,000 if statutory audit mandated

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs; 3.3% social surcharge on corporate income tax exceeding EUR 763,000; research tax credit (CIR), innovation tax credit (CII), and renewable energy tax credit where applicable; no general statutory tax holidays.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (annual cap: EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit above EUR 1,000,000)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 2065-SD (CERFA No. 10272) and annexes (liasse fiscale 2050-2059-SD); electronic filing through EDI-TDFC teleprocedure on impots.gouv.fr professional portal or via an approved EDI partner.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending 31 December: filing no later than the second business day after 1 May of the following year (normally 3 May). For off-calendar fiscal years: within three months of the closing date unless an extension is granted. Electronic filing is mandatory for all companies; paper filing is limited to exceptional situations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: legal form (SARL), corporate name, registered office, SIREN, SIRET, APE/ISIC activity code, intra-community VAT number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the French SIREN assigned upon registration. A non-resident entity with a French permanent establishment (PE) must identify the PE's French registration details and address, not the foreign head office file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal period: opening and closing dates of the accounting year (date d'ouverture and date de clôture).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the actual French statutory accounting period. A non-resident parent may be required to align the PE's taxable period with its own financial year; otherwise the calendar year is applied unless specific approval is obtained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net profit (Bénéfice net imposable) before deduction of loss carryforwards, after statutory add-backs, depreciation adjustments, and transfer pricing corrections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only French-source profit attributable to the French operations. For a non-resident enterprise, include only the PE profit determined under the functional analysis and OECD authorised approach.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net deficit for the fiscal year (Déficit net de l'exercice) if the accounting result after adjustments is negative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete only when Line CA is negative. A French PE may carry forward a deficit to future French tax periods but cannot carry it back unless the profits of the two prior years are within the legal conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year losses deductible against current-year profits (Déficits antérieurs reportables).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Show the loss carryforward utilised, subject to the EUR 1,000,000 fixed deduction plus 50% of the remaining taxable profit. Non-resident PEs must keep supporting documentation available in France and follow the same cap.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: surcharge of 10% of net tax due if filed before formal notice, 40% after formal notice, and 80% for fraudulent intent; late-payment interest of 0.20% per month; a fixed fine of EUR 150 per missing statement; automatic denial of certain deductions; publication and tax lien measures in serious cases.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (Article 119-2 CGI); increased to 75% for payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions (ETNC); reduced under double taxation agreements (DTAs) and potentially exempt under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Claim DTA relief by providing Form 5000 (residence certificate) and Form 5001/5002 (beneficial ownership declaration) to the French paying agent before distribution. If excess tax is withheld, the beneficial owner must file a refund claim with the French tax administration within three years of the payment. EU parent claimants must satisfy the 10% participation threshold for 24 months and submit the relevant directive compliance declaration with the annual filing.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory withholding 33.33%; interest: statutory withholding 50%. Under most DTAs, royalties and interest may be reduced to 0-15%; under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive, related EU companies meeting the 25% shareholding and 24-month holding conditions may receive full exemption.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File triggered when the French entity's net turnover (CA HT) exceeds EUR 50,000,000; Master File triggered when the consolidated group turnover exceeds EUR 750,000,000. Below these thresholds, a taxpayer with cross-border related-party transactions must still be able to demonstrate arm's length pricing upon request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations of the UAE type. However, the general anti-abuse rule (abus de droit, Article L64 LPF) and EU ATAD provisions require real economic substance. A French SARL used as an invoice pass-through without employees, management, equipment, or commercial risk will be disregarded for tax purposes and treaty benefits will be denied for lack of beneficial ownership.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate concealment of project-cargo revenues from the liasse fiscale, issuance of fictitious transportation invoices, or systematic under-declaration of taxable profit on Form 2065.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 80% of the evaded tax for abuse of law; criminal fine up to EUR 750,000; imprisonment up to 5 years (7 years in aggravated circumstances); asset confiscation, seizure of bank accounts, and publication of the conviction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties under Article L267 LPF; criminal courts can impose travel bans, prohibition from managing commercial companies for up to 15 years, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Late Filing / Non-Payment of Corporate Income Tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to submit Form 2065 and annexes by the statutory deadline or failure to pay corporate income tax balances and instalments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late-filing surcharge of 10% of tax due, increasing to 40% after formal notice and 80% for fraud; late-payment interest of 0.20% per month; fixed fine of EUR 150 per missing statement; tax lien against the company's real property.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant may be personally assessed for unpaid corporate tax when insolvency results from mismanagement or intentional default; travel bans can be issued under the tax enforcement procedure to prevent directors leaving France with assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Invoicing international heavy-haul logistics services at non-arm's length rates, undercharging a foreign parent to shift profit outside France, or overpaying an offshore service provider for purported management fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment under Article 57 CGI at arm's length pricing plus 0.20% monthly interest; penalty of 40% for deliberately inaccurate pricing; absence of Local File or Master File triggers an additional fine of up to EUR 10,000 per missing document; publication of the adjustment may be ordered.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign artificial transfer pricing agreements can be held civilly liable for the resulting tax deficiency; criminal prosecution for fraud or money laundering can lead to imprisonment and a travel ban.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a French SARL with no genuine operational substance (no employees, no physical office, no project management functions, no ownership of cargo handling equipment) solely to issue invoices for foreign project cargo activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the SARL under Article L64 LPF; re-attribution of taxable profits to the actual beneficiary; 80% penalty on the evaded tax; denial of DTA benefits; additional EUR 10,000 fine for non-declaration of beneficial owners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced when the SARL is a sham; directors become personally liable for the entire tax debt, may be forbidden from leaving French territory, and risk imprisonment of up to 5 years for fraudulent declaration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the beneficial owner declaration in the French Trade and Companies Register or continuing to accept third-party milestone wire payments without identifying the ultimate beneficiary despite suspicious red flags associated with trade-based money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to EUR 10,000 for non-declaration of beneficial owner (up to EUR 50,000 for legal entities); if money laundering is established, criminal sanctions of 5 years' imprisonment and EUR 375,000 fine for natural persons; asset forfeiture orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly facilitate suspicious cross-border payments can be prosecuted as accomplices to money laundering; civil liability for damages, travel bans, and restrictions on managing commercial entities may be imposed.
